rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality expanded blastocyst and acknowledges image limitations, but it is somewhat noncommittal and includes speculative details (e.g., Gardner 3–4 AA, zona comments) that are not firmly supported from a single still image.

Integrates age, AMH, endometriosis, prior IVF failure, endometrial thickness, BMI, and semen parameters well, and appropriately frames reduced reserve as more relevant to future planning than this transfer.

Reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with a logical link from embryo quality and patient factors to prognosis; minor looseness comes from broad probability framing and some speculative morphology comments.

Mostly aligned with evidence-based IVF practice, including support for single embryo transfer and caution about add-ons, but some recommendations are less guideline-grounded or imprecise (e.g., endometriosis management suggestions, protocol modification examples).

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, avoiding unsupported add-ons, and future evaluation if repeated failure occurs; could be more specific on endometriosis-directed transfer optimization.
